system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of this note:** Internal advice. The Seller's documents are the counterparty's draft and have been tested against our playbook, not accepted as a baseline.

**Headline:** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced" from our perspective. It departs from our playbook on almost every point, and several departures are structural – they would collapse the separate Fundamental/Title and fraud regimes into the general warranty cap and time bar. Three items (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses) go to whether Completion can safely occur at all. The Disclosure Letter is more useful than the Update draft: it candidly confirms that the key deliverables are *not* in the data room, which strengthens our position on each.

---

## Part A – Material issues, in priority order

### 1. Fundamental / Title claims folded into the general regime — **reject outright**

**Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties "subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity"; any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (Cl 12.3/13); limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature" (Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).

**Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.

**Reasoning:** This is the most consequential departure. If title fails, we have paid AUD 24m for shares we do not own; a 20% cap and 18-month bar on that claim is commercially absurd. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. The three clauses operate together: Cl 13's default rule ("unless expressly stated otherwise") plus Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5's "all Claims of any nature" is a hidden general-regime override of exactly the kind the playbook tells us to keep out. Note also the Seller's Tax/IP line ("settled under the general regime above") – this is the same override applied to two categories the playbook says remain OPEN.

**Push-back:** Insert an express carve-out clause: Fundamental Warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances), Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants each have their own regime and are expressly excluded from Cl 12.1–12.3, 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5. Reverse the Cl 13 default so that limitations apply *only* where expressly stated.

### 2. Fraud / wilful concealment carve-out is absent — **non-negotiable**

**Seller position:** No fraud carve-out anywhere; "all Claims of any nature" language would purport to cap and time-bar fraud claims and apply non-reliance to fraudulent statements.

**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. No one on our side may waive this.

**Reasoning:** Beyond the playbook, a clause purporting to exclude liability for one's own fraud is of doubtful enforceability in NSW, but we should not rely on a court to fix the drafting. The absence is itself a signal – it is standard market practice and its omission from a "fair and balanced" package is notable.

**Push-back:** Add an express carve-out at the head of Clause 12 to the maximum extent enforceable. This is a deal-breaker, not a trading chip.

### 3. General warranty cap — 20% is their opening, not our fallback

**Seller position:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. 20% is a fallback available **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. **None has been given.**

**Reasoning:** The Seller's number happens to coincide with our conditional fallback. The team must not treat that coincidence as acceptance. Our mark-up goes back at 25%; if the team later wants to trade down to 20% it requires Amelia Frost's written sign-off referencing this specific draft (SPA-003 / Seller Update) before anything is communicated to the other side.

**Push-back:** Mark up to 25% / AUD 6,000,000.

### 4. Thresholds — five times our de minimis, five times our basket, and excess-only recovery

**Seller position:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; recovery of excess above basket only (deductible).
**Playbook:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded).

**Reasoning:** Three separate departures. The shift from tipping to deductible is the most valuable to the Seller and the easiest to overlook because it is one phrase ("only the excess"). On a business with ~AUD 12m revenue, an AUD 25k de minimis would exclude a large proportion of realistic claims entirely.

**Push-back:** Revert all three to playbook. If a trade is needed later, the basket amount is the least damaging concession; the tipping mechanism and the de minimis should hold.

### 5. Claims period — 18 months with no authority

**Seller position:** 18 months.
**Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

**Push-back:** Revert to 24 months. Same authority point as the cap – the Seller's figure matching our fallback does not authorise us to accept it.

### 6. Disclosure — whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure — **reject**

**Seller position:** Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]: every matter in the data room as at 22 Sept 2026, DD-002 to DD-012, the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" are all generally disclosed.
**Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search disclosure.

**Reasoning:** General data-room disclosure effectively converts the warranties into a disclosure exercise – anything buried anywhere in the room qualifies every warranty. "Publicly searchable corporate records" is open-ended and includes material we have not been given. The Seller's own paragraph [1.4] compounds this: they disclose everything while admitting nothing, so the disclosure protects them without informing us. The specific disclosures in sections 2–10 are acceptable in form (they are fair, specific and candid) and should be the *only* operative disclosures.

**Push-back:** Delete [1.1] and [1.2] and the corresponding Schedule 7 general disclosure. Replace with a standard: a matter is disclosed only if fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Accept sections 2–10 as specific disclosures, subject to the comments below.

### 7. Buyer knowledge exclusion (Cl 8.3) — **delete**

**Seller position:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
**Playbook:** Delete blanket exclusions; any qualifier must be seller-side (named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry); never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**Reasoning:** This clause is the general-disclosure problem restated in a second place, and it is wider: "discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge test, and extending it to advisers means the Seller could run a defence based on what a junior reviewer at our law firm theoretically read. Combined with items 1 and 6 it would leave very little warranty protection standing.

**Push-back:** Delete Cl 8.3 entirely. If the Seller insists on a knowledge concept, it should be their warranty qualifier ("so far as the Seller is aware", with named individuals and a reasonable-enquiry obligation), not a buyer-side bar – and in any event it must not touch title, capacity, fraud or the specific indemnities.

### 8. Bluefen consent — condition is drafted so it can never fail

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours; consent "treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." Disclosure Letter s.2: ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%), change-control cl 11.2 with conditions in 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence conditions are satisfied** in the data room.
**Playbook:** Effective consent *and* evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient for a material customer.

**Reasoning:** Bluefen is ~30% of revenue – this is a value-critical condition. The Seller's drafting has two gaps. First, "satisfied on delivery" means a conditional consent (e.g. consent subject to 11.3 conditions that are never met) counts as full satisfaction. Second, "reasonable endeavours" gives the Seller no real obligation to procure the consent and, if they fail, the deal-risk sits with us. The Disclosure Letter confirms neither consent nor condition-satisfaction evidence exists today, so the condition is live and unsatisfied.

**Push-back:** Condition precedent: written, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2/11.3, in a form approved by the Buyer, with evidence of satisfaction of each 11.3 condition, delivered before Completion. Seller to use all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours (as a minimum, an obligation to take specified steps). Buyer right to waive only in writing. Consider whether a specific indemnity or price adjustment is needed if Bluefen's consent is conditional on commercial concessions.

### 9. Riverlark — post-completion release of AUD 3.2m secured debt is unacceptable

**Seller position:** Release "to be provided following Completion." Disclosure s.3: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2; not repaid; no discharge in data room.
**Playbook:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable bank undertaking *plus* Amelia Frost approval.

**Reasoning:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal we would be paying full price for a company that still carries AUD 3.2m of secured debt with a change-of-control trigger (cl 8.1). If the bank calls on 8.1 after Completion and the release has not been delivered, the exposure is ours. The security also makes our title (indirectly) and the company's assets encumbered on day one.

**Push-back:** (a) Payout letter from Riverlark addressed to the Buyer, current to the Completion date; (b) repayment direct from Completion funds via the funds flow, as a deduction from the price under the debt-free mechanics; (c) executed PPSR discharge, release of any mortgage/guarantee and deed of release delivered at Completion. If the Seller cannot deliver releases at Completion, the fallback is an irrevocable undertaking from the bank to release on receipt of the payout – and that fallback needs Amelia Frost's approval before we offer it.

### 10. Employee bonuses (DD-005) — AUD 420,000 silently omitted from funds flow

**Seller position:** "A matter for the Seller," not itemised in funds flow. Disclosure s.5: AUD 420,000 conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not in the draft funds flow**; silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.

**Reasoning:** "A matter for the Seller" is not a drafting position; it is an assurance with no mechanism. The bonuses are triggered by Completion, so they are a transaction cost the Seller is causing. If they are not itemised and funded, Paperbark (i.e. our company post-Completion) pays them out of its own cash plus on-costs – super at the current rate on top, payroll tax, and potentially leave loading. On AUD 420k the on-costs alone could exceed AUD 60k. The Seller's "continued employment" condition also deserves attention: if the bonuses are structured so that payment falls after Completion, the obligation sits with us even more clearly.

**Push-back:** Specific line item in the funds flow: AUD 420,000 plus a Seller-confirmed on-cost figure, treated as Transaction Debt and deducted from the price, or paid by the Seller directly before Completion with evidence. Warranty and specific indemnity that no other Completion- or change-of-control-triggered employee payments exist.

### 11. Ironquay IP (DD-004 / DD-010) — indemnity is too narrow

**Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate." Disclosure s.4: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 open per DD-010; not independently bank-verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
**Playbook:** Broaden the indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.

**Reasoning:** The real risk is not the AUD 180k; it is that the SOW3 Project Materials have not transferred and Paperbark does not own IP it may be using commercially. An indemnity for the payment amount does not cover (i) loss if the materials are not assigned, (ii) third-party claims from Ironquay, (iii) cost of re-procuring or re-developing, or (iv) any revenue dependent on that IP. The AUD 180k figure comes from a ledger (DD-010) – we should not assume it is right or wrong.

**Push-back:** Broaden Cl 11.1 to cover all loss arising from the Ironquay arrangements including non-transfer of SOW3 Project Materials, any claim by Ironquay, and any payment required to secure transfer. Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay (this is the "cure" to preserve). Request bank evidence of what has actually been paid.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (DD-006) — Seller's "not expected to be material" is premature

**Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material. Disclosure s.6: link to unintended external address, ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); access, scope and notification requirement all undetermined; investigation preliminary; no confirmed breach, no loss figure.
**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.

**Reasoning:** Neither side can characterise this yet, and we should not do so either. The Seller's "not expected to be material" is an opinion on an incomplete investigation. What matters is process: logs must be preserved now (access logs on the link are the only way to establish whether the file was opened), and we need visibility through to Completion. The Disclosure Letter's framing is appropriately neutral and we should hold both sides to that neutrality.

**Push-back:** Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all logs and evidence; complete the investigation with a written report to the Buyer; notify the Buyer of any material development; Buyer consultation on any decision regarding regulator or data-subject notification. Specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident, uncapped by the general regime (or separately capped) – framed around the event, not around an assumed breach. Do not put a number on it.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000) — assess, don't reclassify yet

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure s.8: three related renewals of AUD 110k each; DD-008 and DD-011 to be read together; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

**Reasoning:** The Seller asserts "ordinary course" but their own disclosure declines to say so. Three identical AUD 110k renewals that must be "read together for timing/scope" suggests they may be a single AUD 330k commitment split across documents – which raises questions about whether it was structured to sit below an approval threshold, whether it is accrued at Completion, and whether it is terminable. None of that is established.

**Push-back:** Diligence request: renewal dates, termination rights, whether any amount is accrued or prepaid at the locked-box/Completion date, and the business reason for the three-way split. Hold the question of Debt treatment or working-capital adjustment open until answered. Do not concede "ordinary course" in the SPA definitions.

### 14. Title — share register is not independent evidence

**Seller position:** Title evidenced by the register at DD-012. Disclosure s.10 (helpfully) says this identifies the Seller's source and does not state the Buyer has verified it.
**Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source.

**Reasoning:** The register is maintained by the company the Seller controls. It does not prove the shares are unencumbered (Riverlark's security may extend to shares), that prior transfers were validly executed, or that Harbourglass has authority to sell.

**Push-back:** ASIC company extract; PPSR search against the company and the Seller; review of constitution and prior transfer documents; Seller board/shareholder authority resolutions; Fundamental Warranties on title, capacity and no encumbrances; Completion deliverables including original share certificates (or lost-certificate indemnity) and an executed transfer. All under the separate Fundamental regime (item 1).

### 15. Tax / IP "settled" — they are not

**Playbook:** OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

**Push-back:** State expressly in our response that Tax and IP warranty regimes remain under negotiation and are not accepted as falling within the general cap. Do not over-reach by demanding unlimited liability either – park with a placeholder separate regime to be negotiated.

### 16. Lesser points to note

- **Office lease (s.7 / DD-007):** Notification only, not consent, per the disclosure. Accept, but add a Completion deliverable: evidence the notification was given.
- **Mossvale (s.9 / DD-009):** Assignment restriction; disclosure says a share sale alone does not require consent. Verify the clause ourselves (change-of-control vs assignment wording) rather than relying on the Seller's reading.
- **Disclosure Letter [1.4] and s.11:** Standard no-admission language; acceptable so long as the general-disclosure paragraphs are removed. The s.11 reservation is actually helpful – the Seller concedes we must evaluate the facts ourselves, which cuts against any argument that we "knew" of a matter via general disclosure.

---

## Part B – Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller draft | Our mark-up | Authority needed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fundamental/Title regime | Same as general | Separate: 100%, ≥6 yrs, outside basket/de min/knowledge | None – reject |
| 2 | Fraud carve-out | Absent; "all Claims of any nature" | Full carve-out from caps, baskets, time, exclusive remedy, non-reliance | None – cannot be waived |
| 3 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | 20% needs Amelia Frost written authority identifying this draft – **not given** |
| 4 | De minimis / basket | AUD 25k / 250k / excess-only | AUD 5k / 50k / tipping | None |
| 5 | Claims period | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months needs Amelia Frost written approval – **not given** |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers | Specific fair disclosure only; delete [1.1], [1.2], Sch 7 general | None |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge (Cl 8.3) | Blanket bar incl. advisers / "discoverable" | Delete; any qualifier is seller-side, named persons + enquiry | None |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | CP: effective consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met, before Completion | None |
| 9 | Riverlark | Release after Completion | Payout, direct repayment from funds flow, releases at Completion | Post-completion fallback needs bank irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval |
| 10 | DD-005 bonuses | Not itemised, "matter for Seller" | Line item: AUD 420k + on-costs, Seller-funded / price-deducted | None |
| 11 | Ironquay | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Broaden to all loss incl. non-transfer; evidence of payment + confirmatory assignment | None |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, report, consult; event-based specific indemnity; no figure | None |
| 13 | Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | Diligence questions; no Debt classification yet | None |
| 14 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent ASIC/PPSR/authority evidence + Fundamental Warranties | None |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled under general regime" | Expressly OPEN; separate regime placeholder | None |

**Order of engagement with the Seller:** Lead with items 1, 2, 6, 7 as structural (these are the ones that would gut the warranty package in combination), then 8, 9, 10 as Completion-mechanics items the Seller's own Disclosure Letter concedes are outstanding. Items 3, 4, 5 are the commercial numbers and are best held until the structural points are resolved, so we are not trading cap percentages while the Seller is still trying to apply the cap to title and fraud.

**Internal action items before responding:**
1. Confirm with Amelia Frost that no fallback authority has been or will be given on the cap or claims period at this stage, so the team's mark-up is unambiguous.
2. Issue supplementary diligence requests: Bluefen consent status, Riverlark payout letter, Ironquay payment evidence, Sandbar renewal terms, DD-006 investigation report, ASIC/PPSR searches.
3. Prepare a funds-flow mark-up showing Riverlark repayment and DD-005 bonuses (with on-cost estimate) as price deductions.

I can draft the Clause 12 / 13 carve-out language and the response letter to Seller's counsel if that would be useful next.
=== END ADVICE ===
